plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 (24-layer HfO2/SiO2 stack) based on prior iteration results showing best_target_score improvement from 0.53 to 0.74. Three complementary routes proposed: (1) relaxed thickness bounds with perturbation per feedback directive, (2) increased layer count to 26 for enhanced spectral separation, (3) quarter-wave initialized 24-layer with band-center optimization. All routes maintain parent_route_id: route_01 per refinement chain requirement. Execution requests made fully standalone by explicitly stating all baseline parameters.

routes.title: 24-Layer HfO2/SiO2 Stack with Relaxed Bounds and Coordinate Perturbation
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Relaxing thickness bounds by ±10% and applying deterministic coordinate-wise perturbation of ±4.0 nm to worst-performing 25% of candidates will increase valid candidate density above 10 and escape local symmetry clusters, leading to improved best_target_score.
routes.design_principle: Maintain the verified 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 topology from prior iterations while expanding the search space through bound relaxation and symmetry-breaking perturbations to explore untrapped interior regions of the parameter space.

coordinate-wise perturbation ±4.0 nm on worst 25% candidates

routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 dielectric coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2(1)|SiO2(2)|HfO2(3)|SiO2(4)|HfO2(5)|SiO2(6)|HfO2(7)|SiO2(8)|HfO2(9)|SiO2(10)|HfO2(11)|SiO2(12)|HfO2(13)|SiO2(14)|HfO2(15)|SiO2(16)|HfO2(17)|SiO2(18)|HfO2(19)|SiO2(20)|HfO2(21)|SiO2(22)|HfO2(23)|SiO2(24). Initialize thicknesses from baseline values [127.0, 100.0, 121.0, 100.0, 124.0, 178.0, 96.0, 153.0, 116.0, 152.0, 111.0, 101.0, 140.0, 100.0, 116.0, 144.0, 124.0, 100.0, 117.0, 166.0, 104.0, 100.0, 116.0, 108.0] nm. Relax all thickness bounds by ±10% from baseline bounds of 80-400 nm. Apply deterministic coordinate-wise perturbation of ±4.0 nm to worst-performing 25% of candidates each iteration. Use coherent smatrix solver across combined 300-1700 nm wavelength range. Optimize for mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band and mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band simultaneously. routes.revision_reason: Per feedback directive: relax thickness bounds by ±10% to recover valid candidate density above 10, apply deterministic coordinate-wise perturbation of ±4.0 nm to worst-performing 25% of candidates to break local symmetry clusters.

routes.title: 26-Layer HfO2/SiO2 Stack for Enhanced Spectral Separation
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 24 to 26 provides additional degrees of freedom for spectral separation between UV reflection band (300-450 nm) and SWIR transmission band (1000-1700 nm), potentially improving best_target_score beyond the 0.74 achieved with 24 layers.
routes.design_principle: Extend the proven alternating HfO2/SiO2 topology by adding one additional bilayer pair while maintaining the same material sequence pattern, testing whether marginal layer count increase improves dual-band performance within the 30-layer manufacturing constraint.
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers)
design_variables: thickness bounds 80-400 nm per prior iteration
manufacturing_considerations: additional 2 layers increase deposition time but remain within constraint
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack reflectivity increases with layer count per bilayer stack theory
Additional layers provide more optimization degrees of freedom for multi-band design
expected_advantages: Two additional layers may improve stopband reflectance without compromising passband transmission
Tests whether 24 layers was optimal or if marginal improvement exists at 26 layers
known_risks: Additional layers increase total coating thickness and stress
May not provide significant improvement over 24-layer baseline if 24 layers already near optimal

routes.title: 24-Layer Quarter-Wave Initialized Stack with Band-Center Optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Initializing 24-layer stack with quarter-wave optical thickness at band-center wavelengths (375 nm for UV reflection, 1350 nm for SWIR transmission) provides better starting point for gradient-based optimization than uniform or random initialization, leading to faster convergence and higher best_target_score.
routes.design_principle: Apply quarter-wave stack theory to initialize layer thicknesses based on refractive indices and band-center wavelengths, then allow non-quarter-wave optimization to refine for dual-band performance, combining theoretical initialization with numerical optimization.
routes.proposed_topology: 24 finite layers: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate
manufacturing_considerations: quarter-wave initialization may produce more fabricatable thickness values
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory: reflectivity maximizes when optical thickness equals lambda/4
Multi-wavelength HR designs often deviate from quarter-wave for band optimization
expected_advantages: Physics-informed initialization may converge faster than random or uniform initialization
Quarter-wave values provide fabricatable thickness baseline
Tests whether theoretical initialization improves over prior iteration's gradient-initialized approach
known_risks: Quarter-wave at single wavelength may not optimize dual-band performance
May converge to local optimum near quarter-wave solution rather than global optimum
Refractive index dispersion not fully accounted for in simple quarter-wave calculation

routes.revision_reason: Testing initialization strategy: prior iterations used gradient-based optimization without physics-informed initialization; this route tests whether quarter-wave band-center initialization improves convergence and final performance.
